THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MOHAMMAD NAWAZ  ORAL ORDER Crl.P.No.15777/2025 is preferred by accused No.1 and Crl.P.No.5625/2024 is by accused No.2 to 9 to quash the entire proceedings in C.C.No.27807/2019 pending before the learned XXX1 Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore, registered for the offence punishable under Sections 324,
498A, 506 r/w 149 of IPC.
2.
Respondent No.2/de-facto complainant set the law in motion and based on her complaint, case was registered in Crime No.194/2019 of Bagalagunte Police Station, against the petitioners.
NC: 2025:KHC:51235 HC-KAR 3.
An application is filed in Crl.P.No.15777/2025, reporting settlement, signed by the petitioner as well as respondent No.2.
The contents of the application at paragraph No.1 to 5 are extracted hereunder:
"1. We state that, we are the petitioner & Respondent No.2 in the above matter, we know the facts of the case.
Hence we are swearing to this affidavit.

2. We state that, we are Husband and wife and on the account of some misunderstanding between us a complaint came to be registered on the spur of that moment in Crime No.0194/2019 for the alleged Offences Punishable Section 498A,
324, 506 and 34 of IPC before the Bagalagunte Police and pending before XXXI ACMM, Bangalore in C.C. No.27807/2019.
3.

We state that, with the intervention of elders, well- wishers we do not want to prosecute the criminal case as we have amicably settled the dispute in M.C.
No.59/2025 and we do not want to prosecute the criminal case, accordingly we have decided to put an end to the dispute.

sentences.text: That, the Petitioner and Respondent No.2 herein state that, though this joint affidavit is English NC: 2025:KHC:51235 HC-KAR language and our respective counsels have read over to us and explained the contents of the same in the language known to us/Kannada.
5. We state that, we have decided to settle the case without any coercion or threat and the decision is voluntary."
4. Petitioner and respondent No.2/de-facto complainant are present before the Court.
They submitted that a joint petition for mutual divorce was filed in M.C.No.59/2025 before the Senior Civil Judge & JMFC, Challakere and the Court has granted a decree of divorce.

The respondent No.2 acknowledges that the matter has been settled and in terms of the settlement it was agreed that Rs.5,00,000/- was to be given to her and Rs.7,50,000/- each towards maintenance of each children.
She submits that the said amount has been paid by the petitioner.

5. Respondent No.2/de-facto complainant submits that in view of the settlement she is not interested in pursuing the criminal proceedings instituted by her against NC: 2025:KHC:51235 HC-KAR the petitioners in both the petitions and she has no objection to quash the proceedings.
6. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Narinder Singh and Others V. State of Punjab and Another reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466

entities.text: Narinder Singh and Others V. State of Punjab and Another reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: has held

that when the parties have reached the settlement and on that basis,
petition for quashing the criminal proceedings is filed, the guiding factor in such cases would be:(i)
to secure the ends of justice; or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court

. It is further held that the criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves.

7. Considering that the matter arises out of a matrimonial dispute wherein the parties have settled the dispute amongst themselves, no purpose will be served in NC: 2025:KHC:51235 HC-KAR keeping the proceedings pending against the petitioners.

Hence, the following;
 ORDER  (i) The application is allowed.
(ii) Both the petitions are allowed.
(iii) The entire proceedings in C.C.No.27807/2019 pending on the file of the XXXI Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore, are quashed.
